$comment: Fixture-input erratum for #160 row 3. The active TCT is presented back to its issuer: `self_aid` is the TCT's `iss`, and `aud` = `sub` names the presenter, as RFC-AITP-0005 §10.5 expects, so `aud` is not `self_aid` by design. This fixture tests only the grant check (RFC-AITP-0005 §10.1 item 4, run as §10.5 item 6). §10.5 item 3, which establishes the presenter by downstream PoP or a channel binding, is not under test: the fixture supplies neither, and the `verify_envelope` operation runs only the grant check on `requested_capability` (ADAPTER.md). Through `0.3.4-draft` the claims had `iat` 9999996399, in the future; `iat` is now `__NOW_MINUS_3600__`, which the runner mints like every other placeholder. The expected outcome is unchanged.
description: Caller invokes a capability not present in the active TCT's `grants` claim. Receivers MUST reject with POLICY_VIOLATION (RFC-AITP-0005 §10.1 item 4; registry POLICY_VIOLATION). The check is local; no remote lookup is required. The active TCT is a validly signed compact JWS whose issuer is the verifier (RFC-AITP-0005 §10.5); its signature and expiry pass, and only the grant check fails. Presenter authentication (§10.5 item 3) is not exercised by this fixture.
